title: Society of the Future
author: August Bebel
context: Published as a standalone edition of Part III ('The Socialisation of Society') of August Bebel's classic Woman and Socialism (1879), Society of the Future presents one of the most detailed and inspiring Marxist visions of how a post-capitalist socialist commonwealth will organize production, agriculture, education, art, domestic life, and international relations.
relatesToToday: Bebel's concrete blueprint for democratic economic planning, shortened working hours through automation, ecological soil restoration, universal polytechnical education, and the socialization of housework directly addresses contemporary debates over post-scarcity socialism and work-time reduction.
keyTakeaways: Once society socializes the means of production, the universal duty of all able-bodied citizens to work eliminates parasitism and dramatically shortens the working day.
Democratic administration replaces the repressive class state, which gradually withers away as class domination disappears.
Religion is not abolished by police decree, but withers away naturally as social security, scientific education, and human solidarity replace capitalist misery.
Socialized kitchens, mechanized laundries, and communal amenities abolish private domestic drudgery and secure the full emancipation of women.
Scientific agriculture and global cooperation refute Malthusian fears of overpopulation, ensuring abundance and free individual development for all.
